title: CFP Tax Calculation Notes – Comprehensive Case Worked Example
content:
Case 1: Hong Kong salaries tax calculation. Assume an annual salary of HKD 1,200,000, married with no children, and a spouse with no income. Deductions: MPF contributions of 18,000 and self-education expenses of 20,000. Calculate the assessable income and tax payable.
Steps: Assessable income = 1,200,000 - 18,000 - 20,000 = 1,162,000. Progressive tax rates: first 50,000 at 2%, next 50,000 at 6%, next 50,000 at 10%, and the remaining 1,012,000 at 17%. Tax = 50,000*2% + 50,000*6% + 50,000*10% + 1,012,000*17% = 1,000 + 3,000 + 5,000 + 172,040 = 181,040.
Highlighter note: "Hong Kong salaries tax formula: assessable income = income - allowable deductions". Red pen common mistake: "Don't forget to calculate progressive tax rates in brackets; the first three 50,000 amounts have different rates".

Case 2: Property tax calculation. A rental property has annual rent of 240,000, and rates and management fees total 36,000. The standard tax rate is 15%. Assessable value = 240,000 - 36,000 = 204,000. Tax = 204,000*15% = 30,600.
Highlighter note: "Property tax assessable value = rental income - rates and irrecoverable rent". Red pen: "Note: management fees are deductible, but only the portion paid by the owner".

Case 3: Profits tax calculation. A company has profits of 2,000,000, of which 500,000 is exempt offshore income and 100,000 in foreign tax has been paid. The tax rate is 16.5%. Assessable profits = 2,000,000 - 500,000 = 1,500,000. Tax = 1,500,000*16.5% = 247,500. Foreign tax credit limit = 247,500*500,000/1,500,000 = 82,500. Actual credit is 82,500, and tax payable = 247,500 - 82,500 = 165,000.
Highlighter note: "Profits tax credit: the foreign tax credit shall not exceed the tax payable multiplied by the exemption ratio". Red pen: "Exempt income must be supported by offshore evidence, otherwise it cannot be deducted".
